$comment: THE ONE REGISTRY for the proposal system lab's knobs (the X-Bionic rework, 2026-10-10). Read by /test/proposal-system (TS import through lib/proposal-system/variants.ts) and by scripts/capture-proposal-system.mjs (readFileSync). TYPE IDS ARE LETTERS ONLY. THE FIRST VALUE OF EVERY KNOB IS PRODUCTION: PA is every knob at its first value and the control, byte-identical to /arcs/x-bionic/proposal; every other direction is one argument against it; PZ is ADR-155's whole answer at once. Since the merge with the X-Bionic branch (2026-10-10) the first values name the owner's picks there (the band, the case card, the layer opened, his three lines alone) and the second values are ADR-155's directions. On 11 October he picked the approach drawn as one run, read whole, with the two lines after it ("Whole"): both are first values now, and the runway and the rail over the run were deleted with their guards. When the owner picks, the winning values land on the production record and the losing branches are deleted with their guards (ADR-070 U35).

order.label: Order
order.note: current = the page as shipped. narrative = the owner's order of 10 October: about, the vision, the approach, where it plugs in, Loop, two brands, X-Bionic.

interstitial.label: Part opener
interstitial.note: callout = the owner's three lines, each alone on a screen (ADR-153 U4). quote = ADR-155's chapter band: the part ruler over the same line, numbered one to three.

jobHead.label: Job head
jobHead.note: band = ADR-153 U4's low gold band: the title and its mono line on the left, the job's one workstream on the right. mark = that one lit discipline first, the title one size down, the client, where it ran and the date as one mono line under it.

return.label: Loop's return
return.note: case = ADR-153 U5's case card: the record in the jobs' own housing, a lane per role. ledger = the same four rows as returns in the job's vocabulary: a value, a line, a tally.

approach.label: The approach
approach.note: run = production since the owner's pick of 11 October ("Whole"): his eight-step outline drawn as one run (ArcConfigRun), read whole on one screen. The vision's own layer with its four workstream tiles, creative production's tile opened onto its jobs, ads design worked through from its three inputs to the finished ad, the adopted run checked at every step, the skill and the evals written between the runs, and the automated run asking the workstream's owner once. written = the layer written, read whole (the same evening): the vision's stack one altitude down as one static drawing, the host slab, the gold layer with its courses drawn and named on leaders (the skills filled, the evals open), the team's four diamonds on a deck one course higher, Claude's beads along the front edge to the owner's diamond; the three passes a right column, each on a leader to its mark. opened = the lane opened: the plugin beat's console with only the creative-production lane lit, the three passes as marks along it (the team at its head, the courses mid-lane, the beads to the owner at its end), the passes and the lane's skill and evals in the right column. stack = one mono rail over the layer stack: the team on the organisation's slab, the layer appearing with its courses, Claude's runs along its edge. plates = the beat as it shipped before the run (ADR-153): three plates with a verb each and two time bars, in its own words. The runway and the rail over the run came out with the pick.

upstream.label: Longer tasks
upstream.note: off = production since the owner's video of 11 October (the two lanes were 'completely out of place … rounded shapes … a doodle arrow'; the approach's last sentence hands to Loop instead). lines = the owner's two lines as they shipped from the pick of 11 October (outline steps 7 and 8), authored in the lab now. horizon = a second beat on the owned horizon: the team's day upstream, the agent's run reaching up three times.

engine.label: The engine
engine.note: layer = ADR-153 U6, the layer opened: the gold slab the team writes, a lane per skill, X-Bionic's Claude Enterprise under it. pinned = ADR-154 U4's exploded stack on a runway, its slabs and callouts lighting one after another; the face is dropped, because a face and a pin never share a section.

vision.label: The vision
vision.note: console = production: the console with its three plates (the layer, Claude, the models) and its note. team = the console as it ships, the models tier gone and the team on the stack: the host, the lit layer, the four workstreams standing on it with a green diamond each, the host's connectors dropping under it, the three levels lettered beside it, the owner's role under each workstream in the 2×2. phases = three phases read down: one housing cut into three rows that share edges, a mono rail at the left of each (the team, the layer, Claude Enterprise), the same slab at a crop in each (the deck with its people, the layer with its courses, the host with its connectors), one sentence at the right, a flow leader down. Both carry the note's sentence in the head.

directions.name: House
directions.question: the page as it ships, with the owner's picks of 10 and 11 October: does it already read as one argument?

directions.name: Narrative
directions.question: in the owner's order, with the vision first and the layer placed after the approach, does the page read top to bottom?
directions.shape: the reordered sections, every beat as shipped

directions.name: Chapter
directions.question: does a part open better under a numbered ruler than on its line alone?
directions.shape: three chapter bands, the same three lines under the part ruler

directions.name: Mark
directions.question: with one lit discipline and the proof cards' gold band, do the jobs read as the Loop cards' kin?
directions.shape: four jobs on the mark head

directions.name: Ledger
directions.question: do Loop's returns and the jobs' returns read as one language?

directions.name: Written
directions.question: the layer written, read whole and static: does the vision's object one altitude down, with the three passes on leaders beside it, say the layer better than the run?
directions.shape: the approach as the stack at its written state, the passes a right column

directions.name: Opened
directions.question: the lane opened in the plugin's own console, the three passes as marks along it: does the approach read as the engine beat's kin?
directions.shape: the approach as the plugin console with one lane lit

directions.name: Stack
directions.question: does the layer being written, drawn once, say that adoption and automation are one motion, better than the run?
directions.shape: the approach on the stack figure

directions.name: Horizon
directions.question: the stack, then the owned horizon in place of the two lines: does the longer-horizon claim read better as the team's day upstream?
directions.shape: the stack, then the owned horizon

directions.name: Pinned
directions.question: read in nine lit steps on a pinned runway, does the stack say more than the layer opened?
directions.shape: the engine as the exploded stack, pinned

directions.name: The brief
directions.question: ADR-155's whole answer at once: one narrative, chapter bands, marked jobs, one return language, the stack, the pinned engine.
directions.shape: every knob at its second value

directions.name: The team on the stack
directions.question: with the models tier gone and the four workstreams standing on the layer as a team, each with a person on it, does the console say in ten seconds who runs what on what?
directions.shape: the console, its stack three tiers with the team on top, the role under each workstream

directions.name: Three phases, read down
directions.question: read down three rows of one housing, the team, then the layer, then the Claude it plugs into, does the same object at three crops say the order of the work better than one stack?
directions.shape: one housing cut into three rows, the slab at a crop in each, a sentence a row

wave.note: 1470x830 is the owner's MacBook Air, the binding cell (ADR-153); 1440x790 the smaller Air; 1920x1200 where the 880px fill cap engages. Every beat is one screen by content bottom.
